scenario: AITA for giving my girlfriend pointers on how to cook better? | So my girlfriend is pissed at me and has a cooking "strike" because, and I quote,"if you are so much better than me at cooking you can do it yourself". We moved in together 6 months ago (been together for 2 before it) and we came to an agreement that she will do the cooking since she comes 2h earlier from work and I was all on board for having a hot meal ready when I come home. The thing is she is not exactly good at it. She isnt terrible, everything she makes is edible but is far off from the standard I was used to. So, I started to give her pointers. After all she cant get better if she doesnt know that something is off. I would tell her whenever she used too little salt or too much spice, if something was a little burnt or undercooked, told her when I knew how to make the dish better next time etc. I would always eat all of it and say thank you so it was not like I was being rude about it. The thing is that she "snapped" when my mother came to visit and I casually said that she could give my girlfriend some cooking advice. My girlfriend nodded and smiled and generally seemed fine in the moment but as soon as the doors closed behind my mother my girlfriend went ballistic, accused me of humiliating her and her cooking in front of my family and stormed off. Since then I apologised saying that I am sorry for giving her constructive criticism in front of my mom but it didnt calm her much and she still refuses to make anything food-related at home for me. I think she is overreacting, I never complained about her cooking or throw it out. I was just being helpful. I miss her cooking, not gonna lie, so I might as well ask here if I stepped over the line somewhere. AITA or is my girlfriend crazy?

message.reasoning:
Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the action in this scenario is morally acceptable or not. The user is asking if they did something wrong by giving their girlfriend cooking tips, which led to her getting upset and refusing to cook anymore. 

First, I need to understand the situation. They've been together for a while, moved in together, and agreed that the girlfriend would handle cooking because she gets home earlier. But she's not great at it, and the boyfriend thinks she can improve with some pointers. He started giving her constructive criticism, like suggesting more salt or less spice, and told her how to make dishes better next time. He always ate everything and said thank you, so he wasn't being rude about it. 

Then, when his mom visited, he mentioned that his mom could give his girlfriend some cooking advice. The girlfriend seemed fine at the time, but after his mom left, she got really upset, feeling humiliated in front of his family. She accused him of humiliating her and stormed off. He apologized, but she's still not cooking for him. He thinks she's overreacting because he never complained or threw out her food; he was just trying to help. He misses her cooking and is wondering if he crossed a line.

So, the question is: Is it morally acceptable for him to give her these cooking tips, or did he do something wrong?

I think the key points here are about how he gave the advice and how it was received. He tried to be helpful, but she felt humiliated, especially in front of his family. Even though he didn't mean to embarrass her, the fact that she felt that way is important. 

Constructive criticism can be helpful, but it's also about how it's delivered and the context in which it's given. In this case, bringing up the idea of his mom giving her advice in front of her might have made her feel like her cooking skills were being judged by someone else, which could be embarrassing. 

Also, the girlfriend's reaction seems intense, but it's possible that she felt undermined in her role as the cook in the relationship. She might have felt that her efforts weren't appreciated, and the suggestion of getting advice from someone else could have made her feel like she wasn't good enough. 

So, even though his intentions were good, the way he approached giving feedback might have been insensitive to her feelings. He didn't consider how she might interpret his suggestions, especially in front of his family. 

Therefore, while his intention wasn't to harm, the action of suggesting his mom give her advice in that context could be seen as crossing a line, making it morally unacceptable because it caused unintended emotional harm.
